svg.title: The small quantity in (WS2) has the following precise use. The finite suppliers provide it separately for every word in a fixed finite-degree basis and all its signed and conjugated variants. Taking a maximum over finitely many words preserves convergence to zero. Indeed, if ak,w ≥ 0 and δkan k,w →0 for each of finitely many w, then δk maxw an k,w = maxw(δkan k,w) →0. The polynomial prices of the solved columns are (PC12)–(PC13); the rooted insertion and aligned Gaussian estimates provide these centered budgets and the aligned word comparison on the same station. The finite estimates must supply these products at their actual station radius and grid; the grid cannot be altered independently after a comparison has been purchased. Thus varying labels in a bounded finite-dimensional set costs a fixed finite sum of these basis bounds, rather than requiring uniformity over an infinite set of labels.
